mnemonics.title: ABCDE
mnemonics.explain: Always work down the alphabet — airway before breathing before circulation.
mnemonics.scene: Picture alphabet blocks A-B-C-D-E stacked on a trauma stretcher — you can't reach D until A, B, and C are handled.

mnemonics.title: SBAR
mnemonics.scene: Picture a relay race: you sprint up and hand off the SBAR baton to the next runner in four clean steps.

mnemonics.title: PERRLA
mnemonics.explain: Documented as 'PERRLA' when pupils are normal. Unequal/fixed pupils are a red flag.
mnemonics.scene: Picture two matching flashlight beams hitting two round pupils that shrink together — perfectly equal.

mnemonics.title: AVPU
mnemonics.explain: A fast responsiveness check; each step down is worse.
mnemonics.scene: Picture a dimmer switch sliding from bright 'Alert' down to pitch-black 'Unresponsive.'

mnemonics.title: SAMPLE
mnemonics.explain: A quick way to gather the essentials from a client or family.
mnemonics.scene: Picture handing over a lab 'sample' tray that holds six vials — each one a piece of the client's story.

mnemonics.title: DIG FAST
mnemonics.explain: Three or more with elevated mood suggests mania; safety and nutrition are priorities.
mnemonics.scene: Picture someone digging a hole FAST at 3 a.m. — sleepless, grandiose, and spending wildly. That's mania.

mnemonics.title: AEIOU TIPS
mnemonics.explain: A broad checklist when a client is suddenly confused or unresponsive.
mnemonics.scene: Picture the vowels A-E-I-O-U tipping over a confused head — every letter a reason the brain went offline.

mnemonics.title: TORCH
mnemonics.for: Congenital infections that cross the placenta
mnemonics.explain: Infections that can harm the fetus; prevention and screening matter in pregnancy.
mnemonics.scene: Picture shining a TORCH on a pregnant belly to spot the infections hiding inside.

mnemonics.title: 5 F's
mnemonics.explain: Classic risk profile for gallbladder disease.
mnemonics.scene: Picture five F-shaped flags planted on a gallbladder — the classic gallstone patient.

mnemonics.title: CAUTION

letters.m: Change in bowel or bladder habits
A sore that does not heal
Obvious change in a wart or mole

mnemonics.explain: Teach clients these as reasons to see a provider.
mnemonics.scene: Picture a yellow CAUTION road sign — each letter a warning your body might flash.

mnemonics.title: REEDA
mnemonics.for: Assessing a wound or episiotomy for healing
mnemonics.explain: Increasing redness/discharge with edges pulling apart suggests infection or poor healing.
mnemonics.scene: Picture 'reading' a healing wound with a radar (REEDA-r) that scans for five signs.

mnemonics.title: BUBBLE
mnemonics.explain: The routine postpartum check; a boggy uterus or heavy lochia signals hemorrhage.
mnemonics.scene: Picture blowing soap BUBBLEs down a new mom from breasts to bottom — one bubble per system.

mnemonics.title: 5 W's
mnemonics.explain: Match the day post-op to the likely source of a fever.
mnemonics.scene: Picture five W flags on a post-op calendar — as the days pass, the cause of fever moves down the list.

mnemonics.title: APGAR
mnemonics.for: Scoring a newborn at 1 and 5 minutes
mnemonics.explain: Each scored 0–2; 7–10 is good. Pulse is the most important sign.
mnemonics.scene: Picture a newborn getting a report card with five grades — that's the APGAR score.

mnemonics.title: CATS
mnemonics.explain: Low calcium causes neuromuscular excitability (Chvostek & Trousseau signs).
mnemonics.scene: Picture jittery, twitchy CATS with muscle spasms — that's a body low on calcium.

mnemonics.title: HF FACES
mnemonics.for: Early warning signs of worsening heart failure
mnemonics.explain: Teach clients to report these and to weigh daily.
mnemonics.scene: Picture tired FACES gasping on the couch, ankles swollen — heart failure is slipping.

mnemonics.title: GTPAL
mnemonics.explain: A standardized shorthand for obstetric history.
mnemonics.scene: Picture a midwife's ledger with five tally columns — every pregnancy counted in GTPAL.

mnemonics.title: SAD PERSONS
mnemonics.explain: More risk factors = higher risk. A specific plan plus means is high risk — ensure safety first.
mnemonics.scene: Picture a SAD PERSON standing alone in the rain — each risk factor another cloud overhead.
